title: Findable
summary: Search over a writer's own notes, designed for a note-taking app that runs on a laptop with no server. Papers read for it, meeting notes, the design being written, and the drafts it replaced.

documents.path: Papers/Dense versus sparse retrieval on personal corpora
documents.summary: Okonkwo et al. 2024. Dense, BM25 and hybrid retrieval compared on small personal corpora; hybrid wins on long queries, sparse on short keyword ones.
Lindqvist et al. 2025. A distilled 22M cross-encoder reranks the top 50 on a laptop CPU; what it gains and what it costs.
Sato and Brennan 2023. Mining hard negatives for a retriever: the gain, and the point past which mining more of them hurts.
Ferreira et al. 2024. Fixed windows, sentence windows and late chunking compared for retrieval over long documents.
Adeyemi et al. 2025. A small local model rewrites the query before retrieval; helps ambiguous queries, hurts exact phrases.
Zhou et al. 2024. Using a language model as the relevance judge when there are no human labels, and where it goes wrong.
Kickoff. Scope, the no-server rule, the first latency budget.
Hybrid retrieval chosen; reranking deferred until the Lindqvist numbers are in; index size capped.
Latency budget revised for search-as-you-type; conditions for allowing a reranker.
A user interview: what a heavy note-taker actually searches for.
The design being written: goals, indexing, querying, ranking, latency, evaluation.
The pieces and how they connect: indexer, store, query pipeline, evaluator.
Standup: one line each from Dana, Marcus, Ines, Tom.
